topic_text: The value of goods and services produced in the UK.
text:
UK gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have grown by 1.0% in Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2020 for the second consecutive quarter, while the level of GDP in the UK is 7.8% below its Quarter 4 2019 level.

Over the year as a whole, GDP contracted by 9.9% in 2020, marking the largest annual fall in UK GDP on record.

topic_text: How much the production and services industries contribute to economic output.
text:
Monthly production fell by 1.3% between March 2021 and April 2021 meaning output was 3.1% below its February 2020 level, the last month of “normal” trading conditions prior to the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The fall in production was driven by decreases of 15.0% in mining and quarrying, 0.3% in manufacturing, and 0.9% in water supply & sewerage. These were offset partially by a rise in electricity and gas of 0.5%.

Monthly services grew by 3.4% between March 2021 and April 2021 but was still 4.1% below its February 2020 level, the last month of “normal” trading conditions prior to the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The growth in services was driven by a rise in 12 out of the 14 sectors in the index of services, the largest contributions to the growth being from wholesale and retail trade, education, and accommodation and food service activities.

topic_text: Measures of demand in the economy for output that is produced.
text:
In December 2020, retail sales volumes increased by 0.3% when compared with November 2020; resulting in an increase of 2.7% when compared with February's pre-lockdown level.

In 2020 as a whole, estimates of the quantity bought decreased by 1.9% when compared with 2019, the largest year-on-year fall on record.

UK business investment is estimated to have increased by 5.9% between Quarter 3 (July to Sept) 2020 and Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2020; however, it remains 7.4% below its Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2019 levels.

Over the year as a whole business investment has fallen by 10.2%; by comparison, during the 2008 economic downturn, business investment fell by 15.3% between 2008 and 2009.

topic_text: Demand and supply of labour in the economy and how much employees earn.
text: The employment rate was estimated at 75.2% for January to March 2021, 1.2 percentage points down on the year and 0.2 percentage points up on the quarter.
The unemployment rate was estimated at 4.8% for January to March 2021, 0.8 percentage points up on the year and 0.3 percentage points down on the quarter.

Average weekly earnings for employees in Great Britain in nominal terms (that is, not adjusted for price inflation) increased by 4.6% when excluding bonuses, and increased by 4.0% when including bonuses, in January to March 2021 compared with a year earlier. The growth is driven in part by compositional effects of a fall in the number and proportion of lower-paid employee jobs.

topic_text: Changes in prices of goods and services bought by consumers, as well as those bought and sold by producers in the UK.
text: The Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers’ housing costs (CPIH) 12-month inflation rate was 1.6%x in April 2021, up from 1.0% in March 2021.

The rate of output inflation was positive 3.9% on the year to April 2021, up from positive 2.3% in March 2021. Transport Equipment made the largest upward contribution to the annual rate of output inflation.

Input price inflation displayed positive growth of 9.9% on the year to April 2021, up from positive growth of 6.4% in March 2021. Metals & non metallic minerals provided the largest upward contribution to the annual rate of input inflation.

topic_text: UK exports and imports of goods and services and measures of foreign direct investment.
text: Total imports of goods, excluding precious metals, increased by £1.4 billion (3.9%) in April 2021. Total exports of goods, excluding precious metals, fell slightly by £0.1 billion (0.6%) in April 2021 after two consecutive months of growth.

bulletin_title: Foreign direct investment involving UK companies
text: UK direct investment liabilities were £1,287.6 billion in April to June 2016, up slightly from £1,272.4 billion in the previous quarter. FDI liabilities were following a broadly upward trend in previous years, before falling in January to March 2016.

bulletin_title: Foreign direct investment involving UK companies
text: UK direct investment assets were £1,414.7 billion in April to June 2016, up from £1,349.5 billion in the previous quarter. The value of FDI liabilities has fluctuated over the past two years, although remains broadly similar to levels seen in 2012.
